slot.brief: Draw balls/cards without replacement; ask for probability of a described composition (e.g. all same colour or exactly one of a kind); simple fraction counting.

stem: A bag contains $4$ red and $3$ blue balls. If $3$ balls are drawn without replacement, what is the probability of getting exactly $2$ red balls?
working:
$P=\dfrac{\binom{4}{2}\binom{3}{1}}{\binom{7}{3}}=\dfrac{6\cdot3}{35}=\dfrac{18}{35}$

Independent check: Favourable draws: \(\binom{4}{2}\binom{3}{1}=18\); total draws: \(\binom{7}{3}=35\). Thus \(P=18/35\).
solution:
The probability is the number of favourable draws divided by the total number of draws:
$$P=\frac{\binom{4}{2}\binom{3}{1}}{\binom{7}{3}}=\frac{6\cdot3}{35}=\frac{18}{35}.$$
